prompt:
Add a `tasklist` extension: a list item whose text starts with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` followed by a space becomes a task.
- The marker is replaced by `<input type="checkbox">`, `checked` for `x`/`X`, and `disabled` unless the `clickable` option is true (default false).
- The `<li>` gets the class from the `item_class` option (default `task`).
- It works in ordered and unordered lists, nested lists and loose lists, and keeps inline markup after the marker.
Register it so `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` works once installed.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: I added the `tasklist` extension, and `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` now works. The 14 new tests pass, and so does the full suite (1143 tests; the 112 skipped ones are skipped without my change too). flake8 is not installed here, so I could not run it. A list item whose text starts with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` followed by a space gets a checkbox in place of the marker: `checked` for `x`/`X`, `disabled` unless `clickable=True`. Its `<li>` gets the `item_class` class (default `task`). This works in ordered, unordered, nested and loose lists, and inline markup after the marker is kept. Things you might not expect: the default XHTML output writes the checkbox as `<input checked="checked" disabled="disabled" type="checkbox" />`, and only `output_format='html'` gives the short form. The extension runs before inline processing, so `- [ ] [ref]` stays a task with a link instead of the marker being read as a link. It is registered in `pyproject.toml` and the fixture's `entry_points.txt`, and has a docs page, an API reference page, nav and index entries, and an unreleased changelog entry with no issue number, because there isn't one yet.

check.why: task lists everywhere, options, entry point, docs, tests and changelog
